question: Why is the hormone hCG so important right after a fertilized egg implants?

options.A: It triggers the immediate onset of active labor contractions
options.B: It stimulates the rapid production of red blood cells
options.C: It keeps progesterone levels up so the uterine lining stays strong
options.D: It directly causes morning sickness in the expectant mother

explanation: hCG acts like a cheerleader for the corpus luteum, telling it to keep pumping out progesterone so the womb stays cozy and ready for the baby.

question: Why is cerebral palsy described as a non-progressive condition?

options.A: Symptoms always improve steadily without any medical care
options.B: Treatment can completely repair the damaged brain tissue
options.C: The original brain injury does not get worse over time
options.D: The child will eventually outgrow all physical symptoms

explanation: While the physical body changes and challenges may evolve as a child grows, the underlying brain damage remains static. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of providing nutrition care for patients in the hospital?

options.A: Preventing malnutrition and supporting healing
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital food services
options.C: Replacing the need for doctor-ordered diets
options.D: Ensuring patients gain weight during every stay

explanation: Great job! Good nutrition keeps the body strong so it can fight off infections and heal wounds faster.

question: Why do you need to watch the needle site extra carefully after drawing blood from someone with severe liver disease?

options.A: Their veins are usually completely collapsed from chronic fluid overload
options.B: Their skin is too fragile to tolerate standard adhesive tape
options.C: They often have poor clotting due to low production of clotting factors
options.D: Local anesthetics used during the draw can cause severe allergic reactions

explanation: You nailed it! A struggling liver can't pump out enough clotting proteins, meaning your patient is at a higher risk of prolonged bleeding or bruising after a needle stick.

question: Which group usually faces the hardest time moving to safety during an emergency evacuation?

options.A: Elderly individuals and people with disabilities
options.B: Young adults with personal cars
options.C: Trained rescue personnel
options.D: Government officials in the capital city

explanation: Older people and those with physical challenges often struggle to move quickly or hear alerts during a rush. Every little bit of practice counts!

question: What is a 'windshield survey' in community nursing?

options.A: Checking vehicle exhaust fumes to measure air pollution levels
options.B: Observing a community firsthand by walking or driving through it
options.C: Testing the driving vision of commercial vehicle drivers
options.D: Administering a written questionnaire to hospital patients

explanation: Imagine driving or walking slowly through a neighborhood just observing houses, trash disposal, and daily life. That's a windshield survey!

question: Why is the nursing history an essential part of a comprehensive assessment?

options.A: It provides vital details about the child's developmental timeline and home environment
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory investigations
options.C: It diagnoses rare genetic disorders without testing
options.D: It is only used for billing and insurance purposes

explanation: Parents share daily observations that help nurses and doctors understand the full picture of the child's health. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: How often should a bedbound patient typically be repositioned to prevent pressure ulcers?

options.A: Once every twenty-four hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Only when the patient asks

explanation: Turning a bedbound patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable skin areas and maintains blood flow. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h6)

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: The onset of convulsive seizures
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia.

question: What does a very small standard deviation mean for a set of patient temperature readings?

options.A: The readings are closely clustered near the average temperature
options.B: The highest temperature reading was far above normal limits
options.C: There was a major calculation error made during data entry
options.D: The patients have completely different underlying health conditions

explanation: A small standard deviation means everyone's readings are hugging close to the average—very little variation!

question: Which cranial nerve sends signals from the brain to slow down the heart rate?

options.A: Facial nerve
options.B: Optic nerve
options.C: Vagus nerve
options.D: Hypoglossal nerve

explanation: The vagus nerve is the body's main brake pedal, using parasympathetic signals to help calm and slow down the heart.

question: Why are community health programs that teach about local crops so effective at preventing disease?

options.A: They replace the human need for macronutrients
options.B: They empower communities to use accessible foods to stay healthy
options.C: They rely entirely on expensive imported medications
options.D: They eliminate the need for any clinical healthcare workers

explanation: Exactly! Teaching people how to make the best of what's already growing around them builds long-lasting, self-reliant health habits.

question: A visitor bumps the bed and a weight bag touches the floor. What is your very first step?

options.A: Immediately remove the skull pins to prevent further injury
options.B: Document the incident and wait for the doctor's morning round
options.C: Call the physical therapist to readjust the entire bed frame
options.D: Ensure the rope is in the pulley and lift the weight so it hangs freely

explanation: Quick action is key! Just check the rope and make sure those weights are hanging freely again to keep the traction working.

question: Where do the testicular arteries originate from?

options.A: Renal vein branch
options.B: Femoral artery
options.C: Internal iliac artery
options.D: Abdominal aorta

explanation: Because the testes form near the kidneys during embryonic development before descending, their main blood supply stems directly from the abdominal aorta. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h7)

question: When can palliative care start for a patient with advanced cancer?

options.A: At any point during the illness, alongside active curative treatments
options.B: Only when the patient is completely free of all physical pain
options.C: Exclusively during the final forty-eight hours of life in a hospice unit
options.D: Only after all forms of chemotherapy and radiation have failed

explanation: Wonderful to know! Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it can start right from diagnosis to help manage symptoms and boost quality of life.

question: What is the most important thing a nurse should do right after measuring vital signs?

options.A: Document the values promptly and accurately in the patient record
options.B: Memorize the numbers to tell the next shift verbally
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to write everything down
options.D: Throw away the scrap paper to keep things clean

explanation: Exactly! Quick documentation ensures the whole healthcare team has up-to-date information to keep the patient safe.

question: Which viral STI is managed with lifelong antivirals to keep painful blisters under control?

options.A: Herpes Simplex Virus
options.B: Cytomegalovirus
options.C: Human Papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis A Virus

explanation: Herpes simplex causes flare-ups of painful blisters. Antivirals don't cure the virus completely, but they help manage and shorten the outbreaks.

question: A nurse plans to visit a client living in a remote area with a history of unpredictable aggression. What is the safest action?

options.A: Ignore the history of aggression because home environments are safe
options.B: Go together with a colleague and inform the clinic supervisor
options.C: Send a text message asking the client to come to the clinic instead
options.D: Visit alone very early in the morning before the client wakes up

explanation: Traveling with a partner and notifying supervisors are key safety protocols when visiting clients with a history of aggression. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release hormones directly into the blood
options.B: Exocrine glands possess a rich network of fenestrated capillaries
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete substances exclusively onto the skin surface
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers while endocrine glands do not

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems! Because they don't have tubes (ducts), they dump their hormones straight into the bloodstream to travel round the body. You've got this!

question: Which of these is one of Elisabeth Kübler-Ross's classic stages of grief?

options.A: Bargaining
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Revenge
options.D: Forgetfulness

explanation: Spot on! Bargaining is that stage where a person tries to negotiate a different reality. It sits right alongside denial, anger, depression, and acceptance.

question: Roughly how long does the complete cycle of spermatogenesis take in humans?

options.A: About 6 to 9 months
options.B: Exactly 14 days
options.C: About 64 to 74 days
options.D: Exactly 28 days

explanation: The entire transformation from an immature germ cell to a mature spermatozoon takes approximately two to two and a half months. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of purposive sampling in qualitative studies?

options.A: Choosing people randomly from a large national census list
options.B: Ensuring every person in the hospital has an equal chance to join
options.C: Selecting participants who have direct experience with the topic
options.D: Finding participants who disagree with the researcher's hypothesis

explanation: Exactly! 'Purposive' means on purpose—you pick people who actually lived the experience so they can give you the best information.

question: What is a major goal of health education when a community is facing an epidemic?

options.A: Encouraging early health-seeking behavior
options.B: Discouraging people from visiting hospitals
options.C: Increasing community fear of the disease
options.D: Promoting traditional medical practices

explanation: Spot on! Good health education encourages people to report symptoms early so treatment can start before complications set in.

question: How does financial hardship usually change how people seek healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Patients rely entirely on free federal government prescriptions
options.B: Patients bypass local clinics to visit expensive foreign hospitals
options.C: Patients delay seeking care until their illnesses become advanced
options.D: Patients demand immediate surgical interventions for minor pains

explanation: That's correct. Financial constraints often force people to wait and hope symptoms go away on their own, which unfortunately means they often arrive at the clinic very sick.

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is mainly affected in endometritis?

options.A: The inner lining of the uterus
options.B: The lower part of the birth canal
options.C: The outer covering of the ovaries
options.D: The muscular wall of the womb

explanation: You've got this! 'Endo' means inside, and 'metritis' relates to the uterus. So endometritis is simply an infection or inflammation of the inner lining of the womb (the endometrium).

question: What is the primary nursing priority immediately after a patient returns from a cardiac catheterization via the femoral artery?

options.A: Removing the pressure dressing to inspect the exact puncture wound
options.B: Encouraging the patient to get out of bed and walk around the room
options.C: Checking the insertion site for bleeding and monitoring distal pulses
options.D: Administering a large dose of oral potassium supplements immediately

explanation: Arterial access carries a high risk of bleeding and loss of blood flow to the leg, so nurses must frequently check the puncture site and the pulse in the foot. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is the main difference in who goes into quarantine versus isolation?

options.A: Quarantine requires a hospital bed, while isolation happens at home
options.B: Quarantine is for sick patients, while isolation is for healthy travelers
options.C: Quarantine is for exposed healthy people, while isolation is for sick people
options.D: Quarantine is voluntary, while isolation is always forced by law

explanation: The core difference lies in the health status of the person: exposed-yet-healthy for quarantine, and actively ill for isolation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health habits in local communities?

options.A: Cultural beliefs and traditional illness explanations
options.B: Poverty and severe economic hardship
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical resources
options.D: Distrust of the formal healthcare system

explanation: Spot on! Having plenty of free resources helps health programs succeed. Poverty, cultural myths, and distrust are the real hurdles we face.

question: Why do we need intersectoral collaboration (working with other sectors) to achieve good public health?

options.A: Hospitals are solely responsible for fixing bad roads and cleaning rivers
options.B: The Ministry of Health cannot legally operate without approval from finance officers
options.C: Factors like education, agriculture, and housing directly influence overall health outcomes
options.D: Doctors must personally manage farming and school curriculum development

explanation: Health doesn't happen in a vacuum! Good housing, farming, and schools all play a huge role in keeping people healthy.

question: What exactly is a hospital-acquired complication?

options.A: An expected outcome of chronic disease progression
options.B: A negative health event developing during hospital care
options.C: An illness the patient had before admission
options.D: A normal side effect of curative surgery

explanation: You've got this! These are issues that pop up because a patient is in the healthcare setting or undergoing treatment, rather than being there when they first arrived.

question: A nurse manager sees a report saying patient wait times have a very large standard deviation. What does this mean for the clinic?

options.A: The clinic has successfully eliminated all delays in patient care
options.B: The average wait time is dangerously high for every single patient
options.C: Every patient is waiting the exact same amount of time to be seen
options.D: Wait times vary widely, with some patients waiting a very short time and others waiting extremely long

explanation: You nailed it! A large standard deviation means big differences—some patients are seen immediately while others wait forever, showing the clinic's service is quite inconsistent.

question: Finding Escherichia coli (E. coli) in a water sample tells you what?

options.A: High concentrations of industrial heavy metals
options.B: Recent fecal contamination from humans or animals
options.C: Excessive mineral hardness from underground rocks
options.D: A normal and safe level of plant nutrients

explanation: Spot on! E. coli is our warning flag. Its presence proves that waste matter has found its way into the water supply.

question: Why do doctors prescribe antidiabetic medications for patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: To restore normal metabolic balance and lower blood sugar
options.B: To permanently replace the need for dietary modifications
options.C: To stimulate the continuous release of stored glucagon
options.D: To completely cure the underlying pancreatic disease

explanation: You got it! These drugs help keep blood glucose in check to prevent long-term complications, even though they aren't a permanent cure on their own.

question: What happens to the thymus gland as a person grows older?

options.A: It accumulates calcified deposits known as corpora arenacea
options.B: Its pinealocytes transform entirely into hormone-secreting neurons
options.C: It develops hollow colloid-filled follicles similar to the thyroid
options.D: It undergoes fatty involution and gradually shrinks in size

explanation: As we age, the active immune tissue in the thymus slowly gets replaced by fat cells—a natural process called involution. Nothing to worry about, it's just part of normal aging!

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental protection and waste regulations?

options.A: NCC
options.B: NAPTIP
options.C: NESREA
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) is the body making sure environmental laws and waste rules are followed across Nigeria.

question: Why is focusing only on physical injuries in a patient with a disability a problem?

options.A: It ignores other vital dimensions like spiritual health and inner peace
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever leaving the hospital ward
options.C: It breaks hospital legal documentation rules for charting
options.D: It automatically causes physical therapy to fail within days

explanation: When we only look at physical symptoms, we miss the patient's emotional and spiritual pain. Caring for the whole person means looking beyond just the body!

question: What does viewing a patient in their social context primarily involve?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members during treatment
options.B: Recognizing how relationships and living conditions affect health
options.C: Focusing strictly on the diseased organ and laboratory values
options.D: Prioritizing hospital policies over community traditions

explanation: Social context looks at the broader picture of a person's life, including family and living conditions, which deeply influence health outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: An older adult with severe cataracts is admitted to the ward for a routine hernia repair. What is the most important nursing action during admission?

options.A: Insist that the patient read and sign all consent forms independently
options.B: Keep the room doors locked to prevent wandering
options.C: Remove all personal belongings to create a sterile environment
options.D: Orient the patient carefully to the physical layout of the hospital room

explanation: Helping a patient with low vision learn where things are in a new room (like the bed, bathroom, and call button) keeps them safe and prevents accidental falls.

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: What blood pressure reading is used as the standard threshold to diagnose hypertension in pregnancy?

options.A: 130/85 mmHg or higher
options.B: 120/80 mmHg or higher
options.C: 160/100 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: A reading of 140/90 mmHg or higher, confirmed on two separate occasions, defines pregnancy-induced hypertension. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h1)

question: What is a main goal of couples counseling when treating female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Legally binding the couple to a specific treatment plan
options.B: Improving communication and reducing performance anxiety
options.C: Performing physical examinations on both partners together
options.D: Prescribing precise hormonal dosages for the female partner

explanation: You're doing great! Counseling helps partners talk openly, take off the pressure of strict expectations, and grow closer together.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand water microbiology?

options.A: To help trace disease outbreaks and educate communities
options.B: To measure the exact depth of local rivers
options.C: To design large municipal water treatment plants
options.D: To chemically synthesize new antibiotics for hospitals

explanation: Nurses need this knowledge to connect water sources to community illnesses and teach safe hygiene habits. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a common natural chemical preservative?

options.A: Sodium benzoate
options.B: Artificial nitrate
options.C: Common salt
options.D: Sulfur dioxide

explanation: Salt has been trusted for centuries to draw out moisture and stop bacteria dead in their tracks.

question: Why must healthcare resources always be carefully managed and rationed?

options.A: Governments prefer to spend money on education instead of health
options.B: Patients rarely use the medical services provided to them
options.C: Medical equipment is always too expensive to manufacture
options.D: Resources are limited while human healthcare needs are infinite

explanation: You'll see this a lot in practice: money, beds, and staff are finite, but sick patients always need care. That gap means we have to make smart choices! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: Where does the first step of blood filtration happen in the kidney?

options.A: Glomerulus
options.B: Renal pelvis
options.C: Loop of Henle
options.D: Collecting duct

explanation: Great try! Blood pressure pushes water and small particles through a tiny ball of capillaries called the glomerulus to start the cleaning process.

question: What is a recommended nursing intervention to help prevent post-dural puncture headaches?

options.A: Encouraging adequate fluid intake
options.B: Massaging the lower back area
options.C: Keeping the patient walking for hours
options.D: Restricting all oral fluids

explanation: Adequate hydration helps the body replenish cerebrospinal fluid lost during the procedure. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h6)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to break an adolescent's confidentiality?

options.A: When the adolescent is at risk of severe harm or abuse
options.B: Whenever the patient misses a routine appointment
options.C: When the patient's parents demand to know everything
options.D: Whenever the nurse feels like chatting with colleagues

explanation: That's right! Safety always comes first. If a minor faces extreme danger or abuse, a nurse has a duty to step in and protect them.

question: What is the main purpose of filing a separate internal incident report after an adverse event?

options.A: To track systemic trends and guide organizational safety improvements
options.B: To increase the patient's monthly hospital billing charges
options.C: To provide immediate grounds for terminating the involved nurse
options.D: To publish the staff member's name publicly in local newspapers

explanation: Exactly! Incident reports help management figure out why errors happen so the hospital can fix underlying processes and stop them from happening again.

question: A patient after cancer surgery refuses to get out of bed to walk. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Allow the patient to stay in bed all day without moving
options.B: Wait until the surgeon arrives before attempting any movement
options.C: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with recovery
options.D: Explain that early walking helps prevent blood clots and lung problems

explanation: Kind patient education works wonders! A gentle explanation helps them see why moving early is vital for preventing serious issues like clots. You've got the nurse's touch!

question: What is the medical term for fluid volume deficit (low fluid volume)?

options.A: Hypervolemia
options.B: Hypovolemia
options.C: Edema
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Well done! 'Hypo' means low and 'volemia' relates to blood volume. Put them together and you have hypovolemia!

question: Why does severe anxiety or pain interfere with a client's ability to understand health instructions?

options.A: It limits the client's mental capacity to focus on new information
options.B: It forces the nurse to use complex medical terminology
options.C: It prevents the nurse from speaking in a normal tone of voice
options.D: It automatically makes the client deaf to any spoken sound

explanation: When a person is in intense pain or highly anxious, their brain is overwhelmed, making it very difficult to process and retain health teachings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: What does drug non-compliance mean in nursing practice?

options.A: A doctor writing an illegible prescription slip
options.B: A nurse administering the wrong dose of medication
options.C: A pharmacy running out of essential prescribed drugs
options.D: A patient failing to follow a prescribed medication regimen

explanation: Non-compliance simply means the patient is not taking their drugs the way the doctor or nurse instructed them to. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the main use of the Nigerian National Formulary?

options.A: To grade medical students on their pharmacology exam scores
options.B: To record the personal contact details of all licensed doctors
options.C: To provide a list of approved and safe medicines for healthcare use
options.D: To set the retail prices for all retail pharmacies in the country

explanation: Think of the formulary as your official handbook! It lists safe, approved medications you can trust when caring for patients in Nigerian hospitals.

question: What is the primary function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: Anchoring the muscle to nearby bone tissue
options.B: Transmitting nerve impulses along the surface
options.C: Producing ATP through aerobic respiration
options.D: Storing and releasing calcium ions

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum holds calcium ions until an electrical impulse triggers their release to start contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is one well-known disadvantage of giving medications rectally?

options.A: Immediate destruction of red blood cells
options.B: Instantaneous and painful liver failure
options.C: Erratic and unpredictable drug absorption
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the anal sphincter

explanation: Because of stool, different blood flow rates, or early expulsion, rectal drugs don't always absorb as steadily as intravenous medications.

question: A mother knows exclusive breastfeeding is best, but her relatives force her to give the baby water. What type of barrier is this?

options.A: Severe physical exhaustion from hard farm labor
options.B: Social and family pressure influencing behaviour
options.C: An allergic reaction to infant formula milk
options.D: A complete lack of basic literacy skills in the community

explanation: Spot on! Even when someone has the right knowledge, family and cultural expectations can create tough external barriers to healthy practices.

question: What is the primary role of nutrition in clinical nursing care?

options.A: Lowering hospital cleaning costs
options.B: Replacing the need for routine medications
options.C: Accelerating nursing shift handovers
options.D: Serving as a therapeutic tool for healing

explanation: Food and proper nutrition provide the essential building blocks the body needs to repair tissues and fight off disease, making it a key part of medical treatment. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach program in a rural area with high rates of unsafe injections. What should be the main focus?

options.A: Encouraging residents to perform self-injections to avoid clinic queues
options.B: Educating residents on the risks of unsafe injections and the safety of oral alternatives
options.C: Distributing personal sharps containers for families to keep in their kitchens
options.D: Teaching community members how to safely sterilize glass syringes at home

explanation: Community outreach is all about building awareness! Teach people about injection risks and show them that safe oral medicines work wonders too.

question: What is the main purpose of a low-calorie diet?

options.A: Maximizing rapid muscle mass hypertrophy
options.B: Slowing down the basal metabolic rate
options.C: Increasing total daily physical endurance
options.D: Creating an energy deficit for weight loss

explanation: Spot on! A low-calorie diet simply means taking in fewer calories than your body burns, which forces it to use up stored fat for energy.

question: When an endocrine gland responds to 'humoral' stimulation, what is it actually reacting to?

options.A: Direct commands from the cerebral cortex
options.B: Levels of nutrients and ions in the blood
options.C: Electrical signals from the spinal cord
options.D: The presence of circulating releasing factors

explanation: Great job remembering this! 'Humoral' just means the gland is tasting the blood for things like calcium or glucose and reacting to what it finds.

question: Why do nurses stick around and monitor a patient for about 30 minutes after certain shots or vaccines?

options.A: To ensure the patient does not walk around too soon
options.B: To verify that the medication has been fully absorbed
options.C: To measure the exact change in body temperature
options.D: To watch for acute allergic or anaphylactic reactions

explanation: Better safe than sorry! Severe allergic reactions usually pop up fast. Keeping an eye on your patient during that first half-hour means you can jump in with emergency help if needed.

question: Why can myocarditis lead to signs of heart failure?

options.A: Heart valves become completely stuck open by fibrous scar tissue.
options.B: Electrical impulses travel too fast through the damaged heart chambers.
options.C: Inflammation damages the heart muscle cells, reducing their ability to contract effectively.
options.D: Fluid builds up inside the pericardial sac and crushes the coronary arteries.

explanation: When the heart muscle (myocardium) is inflamed, it gets tired and weak, losing its strong pumping power. This causes blood to back up—leading to heart failure symptoms.

question: A teenager living with chronic obesity faces a much higher risk of developing which condition early in life?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Type 2 diabetes
options.C: Type 1 diabetes
options.D: Pernicious anemia

explanation: You got it! Extra body fat makes the body struggle with insulin, putting teens with obesity at a higher risk for type 2 diabetes.

question: Which leadership style involves making all decisions alone and giving direct orders?

options.A: Laissez-faire
options.B: Democratic
options.C: Autocratic
options.D: Servant

explanation: An autocratic leader keeps full control of decision-making and expects strict compliance from the nursing staff. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is advance care planning so important for older adults?

options.A: It guarantees that residents will never experience physical pain
options.B: It ensures the resident's personal wishes for end-of-life care are known and honored
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to communicate with grieving relatives
options.D: It legally forces family members to pay for expensive surgeries

explanation: Talking about preferences early on ensures that future medical decisions truly reflect what the resident wants when they can no longer speak for themselves.

question: On her third day after delivery, a patient complains that her right calf is painful, swollen, and feels warmer than the left. What is the most important thing you should do?

options.A: Encourage her to walk briskly around the hospital corridor
options.B: Massage the calf firmly to break up any muscle cramps
options.C: Apply an ice pack directly to the painful calf muscle
options.D: Instruct the patient to stay off her feet and notify the physician immediately

explanation: This sounds like a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Never massage a suspected clot, as it could break loose and travel to the lungs—always keep the patient resting and call the doctor right away!

question: How does using the nursing process in critical care differ from a normal ward?

options.A: Evaluation of patient outcomes is delayed until discharge to home
options.B: Planning is entirely determined by family members rather than the nurse
options.C: Steps happen in a rapid, continuous, and overlapping loop due to instability
options.D: Assessment is performed only once upon admission to the ICU

explanation: In the ICU, things move super fast! Because patients can crash at any second, you'll find yourself assessing, helping, and checking results almost all at the same time.

question: Why does catching and treating shock early make such a huge difference in saving a patient's life?

options.A: It halts the cellular hypoxic cycle before irreversible organ damage occurs
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never require vasoactive medications
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It stops all natural immune and inflammatory responses immediately

explanation: Time is tissue! Acting fast restores oxygen to starving cells before they reach the point of no return, preventing multi-organ failure and giving the patient a fighting chance.

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for packaged instruments sitting in storage?

options.A: Sterility depends entirely on the specific time of day it was processed
options.B: Instruments lose their sterility the moment they are placed on a shelf
options.C: All items automatically expire exactly seven days after autoclaving
options.D: Items remain sterile until the packaging is damaged or exposed to moisture

explanation: Instead of worrying about a strict calendar expiration date, packs stay sterile as long as the packaging remains safe and dry!

question: As a nurse, why do you need to monitor patients with digestive disorders very closely?

options.B: Intestinal tracts do not connect to other systems
options.C: The gut controls vital fluid and acid-base balance
options.D: Patients with gut problems refuse all medication

question: What are the main parts of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, blood donation drives, and psychiatric isolation
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkages
options.C: Mandatory legal reporting, punitive counseling, and moral interrogation
options.D: Routine hysterectomy, genetic testing, and long-term foster care referral

explanation: PAC is a complete care package: treat the immediate danger, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect them to healthy support networks. Brilliant concept to master!

question: A nurse wants women to turn up for a new maternal health clinic. What is the best first move with local stakeholders?

options.A: Rely entirely on radio announcements without speaking to community leaders
options.B: Start the clinic secretly to avoid drawing unwanted attention
options.C: Impose strict attendance fines for women who miss antenatal visits
options.D: Involve local chiefs and women leaders early to help design the rollout

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with respected local leaders builds instant trust and makes community members eager to participate.

question: What is the primary goal of intra-natal care?

options.A: Achieving a safe delivery for mother and baby
options.B: Ensuring the mother sleeps through delivery
options.C: Speeding up the duration of the first stage
options.D: Preventing the need for any pain relief

explanation: The main focus of intra-natal care is to safeguard the health and well-being of both the mother and the newborn throughout labor and birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: How should a nurse protect a patient's dignity during a bedside handover?

options.A: Speak in a very loud voice so everyone in the hallway can hear
options.B: Ask all family members to permanently leave the hospital ward
options.C: Ensure privacy curtains are drawn and sensitive details are discussed discreetly
options.D: Refuse to let the patient look at their own medical chart

explanation: Always draw privacy curtains and keep your voice soft and respectful when talking about private health matters.

question: What makes patient participation in a nursing research study ethical?

options.A: It must be mandatory for all patients admitted to the ward
options.B: It must offer large financial rewards to guarantee compliance
options.C: It must be completely voluntary with informed consent
options.D: It must be approved by senior nursing staff without patient input

question: A patient is bleeding steadily with dark red blood from a laceration. Which vessel is most likely involved?

options.A: A lymph node
options.B: A capillary
options.C: A vein
options.D: An artery

question: Your CBI patient has bright red drainage and is crying out with severe lower tummy cramps. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Rapid healing of the surgical wound inside the bladder
options.B: A blocked catheter trapping fluid and blood clots
options.C: A normal reaction to room-temperature saline solution
options.D: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic skin wipes

question: What is the main purpose of primary prevention strategies when tackling gender-based violence?

options.A: Punishing perpetrators through strict criminal justice penalties
options.B: Treating physical injuries in the emergency department after an assault
options.C: Providing legal representation for survivors during courtroom trials
options.D: Stopping violence before it occurs through education and community awareness

explanation: You've got this! Primary prevention is all about stopping abuse before it even starts by shifting community mindsets.

question: What makes a family 'vulnerable' in community nursing?

options.A: Living only in rural farming settlements
options.B: Always rejecting nursing advice
options.C: Lacking resources to handle daily stress and crises
options.D: Refusing to join community health programs

question: What happens to the actual length of thick and thin filaments when a muscle contracts?

question: Why do you need to understand how the lymphatic system drains the reproductive organs?

options.A: It explains how menstrual cramps travel down to the legs
options.B: It shows how vaginal pH changes during a bacterial infection
options.C: It dictates the correct dosage for oral contraceptive pills
options.D: It helps track how pelvic cancers can spread through the body

question: How are Type IV hypersensitivity reactions different from Types I, II, and III?

options.A: They only happen inside internal organs, never on the skin
options.B: They are driven by T-cells and take days to develop instead of using fast antibodies
options.C: They destroy red blood cells using complement proteins
options.D: They are only triggered by eating certain foods

explanation: Unlike the other types that rely on quick antibodies, Type IV is a 'delayed' reaction. It relies on T-lymphocytes taking a few days to show up and cause a reaction (like a bad rash).

question: What is the main purpose of innovative 'small-house' models in modern nursing care?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any professional healthcare oversight
options.B: To lower building construction costs by using temporary tents
options.C: To break large, sterile institutions down into homelike residential units
options.D: To reduce the total number of older adults requiring assistance worldwide

explanation: Small-house models ditch the long, intimidating hospital hallways and replace them with cozy, home-style spaces where residents can build genuine community connections.

question: A 16-year-old first-time pregnant girl comes to her first antenatal visit. How should the nurse behave to make sure she comes back?

options.A: Offering a friendly, confidential environment free from moral judgment
options.B: Requiring an older family member to answer all questions for her
options.C: Limiting her visit duration to avoid overwhelming her with information
options.D: Scolding her gently for becoming pregnant at such a young age

question: During which week of enteric fever are dangerous complications like intestinal bleeding or tears most likely to happen?

options.A: Eighth week
options.B: Third week
options.C: Fifth week
options.D: First week

question: Which of these is a factual note rather than a personal opinion?

question: Why might an ethics committee step in and halt a clinical trial early?

options.A: All participants have decided to change their personal lifestyles
options.B: The research team has run out of interesting topics to write about
options.C: The hospital building requires routine maintenance
options.D: The experimental treatment is proven to be overwhelmingly beneficial

explanation: Wonderful logic! If a new treatment turns out to be a life-saver early on, researchers stop the trial so everyone else can benefit right away. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of achieving high community vaccination coverage?

options.A: Ensuring pharmaceutical companies sell enough medication each year
options.B: Preventing chronic non-communicable illnesses like diabetes
options.C: Creating herd immunity to protect vulnerable people who cannot be vaccinated
options.D: Eliminating the need for any handwashing or sanitation practices

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs have a hard time spreading, which keeps fragile individuals safe. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do teenagers often take sudden risks even when they know the dangers?

options.A: They deliberately ignore all forms of social interaction

options.C: They possess completely adult-like cognitive maturity in all situations

question: In pharmacology, what does 'bioavailability' actually tell us?

options.C: The fraction of an administered drug that reaches systemic circulation unchanged

question: What does your body do when your blood calcium levels drop too low?

options.D: Parathyroid hormone stimulates osteoclasts to release calcium from bone

question: How do learning disabilities differ from global developmental delays?

options.C: Learning disabilities affect specific academic areas while overall intelligence remains intact

question: What is the name of the special, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?

question: How would you simply describe a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: Any gestation that lasts longer than thirty-six weeks

options.C: Any pregnancy that occurs in a woman older than twenty years
options.D: A pregnancy where the health of the mother or baby is at increased risk

question: What is the single most important infection control habit in maternity care?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Using plastic floor sheets

explanation: Good old handwashing is your superpower. Soap, water, or sanitizer washes away transient germs and stops infections from spreading.

question: A community action plan includes assigning specific tasks to local youth groups. What is the main benefit of this?

options.A: It guarantees that international donors will send more money

options.C: It eliminates the need for any monitoring or supervision

question: Where do we usually place a peripheral arterial line?

question: Which skin gland secretes an oily substance called sebum?

question: Why is a chest X-ray usually done right after a thoracentesis?

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable voices are heard equally during community meetings?

options.A: Competition
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Delegation
options.D: Equity

question: What factor most heavily influences how well a newborn with a birth defect will recover?

question: What is the primary goal of inhalation therapy?

question: How do anticoagulant medications help treat a deep vein thrombosis?

question: What role does estrogen play right before ovulation?

question: What happens to the white blood cell count during active labour and delivery?

question: What is the main focus of community nutrition compared to hospital dietetics?

question: What is the clock-face method used for during mealtime assistance?

question: Why did older medical books divide these drugs into major and minor tranquilizers?

question: Why are medications like gabapentin or amitriptyline prescribed for some types of chronic pain?

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of pharyngitis?

question: At what exact point should healthcare waste be sorted into different bins?

question: A clinic nurse notices an unusual rise in severe watery diarrhea cases over two days. What should she do first?

question: What is the main goal of doing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after a major safety incident?

question: Why is keeping clear records of vital signs and treatments especially crucial in flight nursing?

question: A nurse makes a medication calculation error because orientation on the new infusion pump was rushed. What is the root cause?

question: What is the correct order of steps in a PDSA quality cycle?

question: A patient has worried endlessly about money for over a year and now feels constantly exhausted and sick. Which GAS stage is this?

question: If a community has high rates of illiteracy, how should nurses adjust their health education strategy?

question: Why should a nurse worry if a patient completely cuts out a major food group?

question: Why do many teenage girls experience irregular periods shortly after starting menstruation?

question: Why is interactive training better for food workers than just reading a textbook?

question: Why do clinical wards need to do regular stock checks of their medicines?

question: Which of these is a common technology-related cause of patient harm in the hospital?

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

question: Which of the following is a major environmental barrier to effective health communication in a clinic?

question: Why is it important to spot financial stress or a lack of resources during a palliative assessment?

question: What is the main public health goal of achieving high herd immunity within a community?

question: During community outreach, a nurse asks a client if they are ready to stop smoking today. Which of the '5 As' is this?

question: How can nurses actively help prevent unsafe abortions out in the community?

question: What is the primary focus of Primary Health Care within a community?

question: Which dimension of quality care ensures that clinical treatments are based on proven scientific guidelines?

question: Which of these is a core responsibility of a nurse in primary health care?

question: What is the immediate correct action if a surgical sponge count is incorrect at the end of a surgery?

question: According to the Nigerian immunization schedule, which vaccine is given to a newborn baby right at birth?

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

question: How is disaster triage different from regular emergency department triage?

question: What is the main purpose of a community diagnosis?

question: When auditors talk about the 'scope' of a management audit, what do they mean?

question: What is the main job of thermoreceptors in the skin?

question: Why do we call vitamins and minerals 'micronutrients'?

question: Why should the head of the bed stay elevated after a stroke patient eats?

question: How often should an emergency nurse reassess an unstable patient?

explanation: When you swallow a pill, the liver catches and breaks down a good chunk of it before it reaches anywhere else (the first-pass effect). So doctors prescribe a bit extra to make sure enough drug survives!

question: What is the main goal of giving post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) right after an accidental needle stick?

options.A: To cure a chronic bacterial skin infection
options.B: To prevent the establishment of a viral infection
options.C: To numb the skin and prevent local tissue scarring
options.D: To relieve muscle spasms around the injury site

explanation: PEP uses quick antiviral meds to stop a virus from taking hold and multiplying after an accidental exposure. Every minute counts!

question: What is the name of the medication commonly used to treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy medically?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Methotrexate

explanation: Methotrexate is a chemotherapy drug that stops rapid cell division, safely ending an early ectopic pregnancy without surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h6)

question: A client asks when it is safe to have sexual intercourse again after an abortion. What is the best advice?

options.A: Wait exactly one full year before trying again
options.B: Resume only during the weekend
options.C: Resume immediately if there is no headache
options.D: Wait until bleeding stops completely and the cervix closes

explanation: Advise 'pelvic rest' until bleeding stops and the cervix closes. This simple rule prevents bacteria from entering and drastically cuts down the risk of infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: Which fetal position is required for a safe home delivery?

options.A: Cephalic presentation
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Oblique position

explanation: The baby must be in a head-down, or cephalic, position for a normal vaginal delivery to proceed safely at home. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h3)

question: A nurse wants to read a new study, but the journal website demands a heavy payment to view it. What kind of barrier is this?

options.A: Patient-related preference barrier
options.B: Personal attitude barrier
options.C: Communication and accessibility barrier
options.D: Clinical expertise barrier

explanation: Spot on! High subscription fees lock away valuable knowledge, making it an accessibility hurdle for busy clinicians.

question: Why are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) so popular for feeding hungry children early in a disaster?

options.A: They have a very short shelf life that forces quick consumption
options.B: They taste sweet and only appeal to adults
options.C: They provide quick nutrition without needing clean cooking water or fuel
options.D: They replace the need for breastfeeding entirely

explanation: When there's no firewood or clean water to cook with, RUTF packets save the day by providing instant, safe nourishment.

question: On a partograph, what does crossing the action line mean for the healthcare team?

options.A: Midwives should wait four more hours
options.B: Immediate medical intervention is required
options.C: The patient is ready for spontaneous delivery
options.D: Labour is progressing at a normal rate

explanation: You've got this! The action line is a clear warning sign that labour is taking longer than expected. It tells us we need to step in and help the mother right away.

question: Why do scientists make semi-synthetic versions of natural antibiotics like penicillin?

options.A: To make the manufacturing process significantly slower and more expensive
options.B: To ensure the drug cannot be absorbed by human gastrointestinal tissue
options.C: To improve stability against stomach acid and broaden antibacterial effectiveness
options.D: To completely remove any chemical similarity to the original fungi

explanation: Tweaking natural penicillin in the lab helps it survive stomach acid and fight off a wider range of stubborn bacteria. Brilliant science!

question: Which of these is a classic example of primary prevention in community health?

options.A: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.B: Conducting blood pressure screening for adults
options.C: Treating complications of advanced diabetes
options.D: Administering routine childhood immunizations

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention stops diseases before they even start. Vaccines are a fantastic way to protect children proactively before germs ever get a chance.

question: A patient with a bad ankle sprain gets a short leg cast. What is the main goal here?

options.A: Enhancing rapid cartilage regrowth in the joint
options.B: Resting the injured joint to reduce inflammation
options.C: Removing excess fluid trapped inside the joint capsule
options.D: Preventing permanent muscle atrophy in the calf

explanation: By keeping the sprained joint still, you stop painful movement and give the damaged ligaments time to rest and heal.

question: What does an 'informed culture' depend on most in daily hospital work?

options.A: Strict rules that penalize any minor deviation
options.B: Leaving safety decisions entirely to hospital directors
options.C: Ignoring small mistakes that do not harm patients
options.D: An understanding of factors affecting safe patient care

explanation: Think of it as staying aware! An informed culture keeps all staff mindful of the everyday things—like fatigue or busy shifts—that can impact how safely we care for patients.

question: Which sterilization method is best suited for sharp surgical blades because it prevents them from dulling?

options.A: Boiling water for twenty minutes
options.B: Dry heat in a hot air oven
options.C: High-pressure steam autoclave
options.D: Cold soaking in mild soap water

explanation: Dry heat does not cause rust or water-related dulling, making it ideal for maintaining the sharp edges of surgical blades. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Which serious kidney complication is linked to severe E. coli O157:H7 food poisoning?

options.A: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
options.B: Chronic pulmonary fibrosis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Ascending motor paralysis

explanation: Spot on! Certain strains of E. coli like O157:H7 release toxins that can wreck blood vessels and lead to a serious kidney condition called hemolytic uremic syndrome.

question: A nurse makes a drug dosage mistake and now gets very nervous and avoids preparing intravenous medications. What is this behavior called?

options.A: Aggressive confrontation of peers
options.B: Intentional insubordination to management
options.C: Professional indifference and apathy
options.D: Hypervigilance and avoidance behavior

explanation: It's natural to want to run away from tasks that remind us of a painful mistake. Identifying this avoidance helps us address the fear rather than just hiding from it.

question: A patient notices he cannot get an erection anymore shortly after starting a new blood pressure drug. How would you classify this?

options.A: As an age-related normal variant
options.B: As a secondary sexual dysfunction
options.C: As a primary sexual dysfunction
options.D: As an inherited congenital anomaly

explanation: Spot on! Because his sexual function was fine before starting the medication, this is classified as a secondary issue tied to the new drug.

question: A sudden outbreak of watery diarrhea hits a village. As a community nurse, what is your very first step?

options.A: Report the cluster promptly and investigate potential water sources
options.B: Prescribe strong antibiotics to every single person in the village
options.C: Advise villagers to stop drinking all liquids for several days
options.D: Wait patiently until the local hospital requests formal assistance

explanation: Spotting the pattern, reporting it quickly, and hunting down the water source stops cholera and similar outbreaks in their tracks!

question: What is considered the most reliable indicator of a patient's pain intensity?

options.A: The nurse's clinical observation of vital signs
options.B: The physical size and depth of the tissue injury
options.C: The family member's estimate of the discomfort
options.D: The patient's personal self-report

explanation: Pain is a subjective experience, making the direct word of the patient the single most reliable source of information. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h3)

question: What is the main focus of a physical therapist visiting a patient at home?

options.A: Providing emotional counseling for grief
options.B: Assisting with daily grocery shopping
options.C: Restoring physical mobility and strength
options.D: Managing complex intravenous drug dosages

explanation: Correct! Physiotherapists help patients get moving again so they can regain their balance and daily strength.

question: You just received a new supply of liquid pentavalent vaccines for your clinic fridge. Where should you place them?

options.A: Packed tightly inside the door racks in multiple layers
options.B: On the middle shelves, away from freezer walls
options.C: Inside a sealed container filled with unconditioned ice
options.D: Directly touching the floor of the freezer compartment

explanation: Pentavalent vaccines hate freezing! Keep them safely on the middle shelves where the temperature stays stable and above freezing.

question: What physical feature is most commonly seen in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Permanent low blood pressure and dehydration
options.B: Central obesity with a round 'moon face'
options.C: Dark bronze hyperpigmentation of the skin
options.D: Severe weight loss and profound muscle wasting

explanation: Too much cortisol changes how fat is stored in the body, leading to a characteristic round 'moon face' and extra weight packed around the trunk and upper back.

question: Why is routine clamping of a chest tube strongly discouraged when moving a patient?

options.A: It permanently ruins the plastic collection chambers of the unit
options.B: It increases the risk of severe infection at the insertion site
options.C: It can quickly cause a life-threatening tension pneumothorax
options.D: It causes the sterile water in the seal chamber to evaporate

explanation: Clamping traps air and fluid with nowhere to go. This can cause the lung to collapse rapidly, so avoid clamping unless ordered for specific tests!

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?

options.A: 60 percent
options.B: 5 percent
options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 20 percent

explanation: Water makes up about 60% of an adult body! It is the fluid highway where almost all cellular activities happen.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to ensure a patient can safely manage complex wound care and dressing changes at home?

options.A: Tell the patient to wait until the wound heals entirely on its own
options.B: Assume the family knows what to do because dressing changes are simple
options.C: Ask the patient to read a medical textbook chapter before leaving the hospital
options.D: Provide written instructions and have the patient demonstrate the technique back

explanation: Return demonstration combined with written instructions ensures the patient or caregiver actually understands and can perform the steps correctly at home. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h8)

question: What is a major safety challenge unique to home health nursing compared to working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Working alone in unsupervised, unfamiliar community environments
options.B: Lacking access to electronic health charting systems entirely
options.C: Being barred from performing physical assessments on patients
options.D: Having no responsibility for coordinating multidisciplinary care

explanation: Unlike the structured hospital ward where colleagues are close by, home health nurses often travel and enter private homes completely on their own.

question: You hear gurgling sounds and see thick secretions in an unconscious patient's mouth. What is your very first action?

options.A: Turn the patient flat on their back and offer water
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Wait for the doctor to arrive before doing anything
options.D: Suction the airway to clear out the secretions

explanation: Brilliant! Gurgling means the airway is blocked. Grab that suction machine right away to help them breathe easy again.

question: As a nurse, what is one of your most important duties right before the patient goes for surgery?

options.A: Verifying that the informed consent form is signed
options.B: Teaching the patient how to change their wound dressing
options.C: Ordering a special post-operative hospital diet
options.D: Scheduling the patient's follow-up clinic appointment

explanation: Great job! Making sure the consent form is signed proves the patient understands the surgery, its risks, and has agreed to it before heading to the theater.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an allergic reaction after administering eye drops?

options.A: A slight bitter taste in the back of the mouth
options.B: Mild coolness on the surface of the skin
options.C: Sudden swelling and itching around the eye
options.D: Temporary blurriness right after the drop falls

explanation: Swelling, intense itching, and hives indicate an allergic immune response to the medication ingredients. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: Which set of lab tests is primarily ordered to check how well the thyroid gland is working?

options.A: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.B: Morning cortisol and ACTH levels
options.C: Fasting glucose and HbA1c levels
options.D: TSH, T3, and T4 levels

explanation: Spot on! Checking TSH (the boss hormone from the pituitary) along with T3 and T4 (the actual thyroid hormones) gives a complete picture of thyroid health.

question: How does a community-level nursing diagnosis differ from an individual patient diagnosis?

options.A: It is written by traditional rulers instead of trained nursing personnel
options.B: It ignores environmental factors and concentrates purely on gene mutations
options.C: It describes health patterns and risks affecting an entire group or population
options.D: It focuses only on surgical complications inside a hospital operating theater

explanation: Community nursing diagnoses address population-wide health issues and collective responses rather than single patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: How does family planning directly promote gender equality?

options.A: By making biological differences between men and women disappear
options.B: By giving women control over their reproductive lives so they can pursue education and work
options.C: By ensuring that only women make decisions regarding community finances
options.D: By legally prohibiting men from participating in healthcare discussions

explanation: Fertility control frees women from the cycle of constant childrearing, enabling them to pursue personal and professional goals on equal footing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: What is the most common condition treated using genito-urinary anticholinergics?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Overactive bladder
options.D: Kidney stone formation

explanation: Overactive bladder—marked by sudden, intense urges to pee—is the number one reason these drugs are given.

question: How should you as a nurse organize your questions when running through a review of systems?

options.A: Let the patient talk freely without any guided direction
options.B: Ask targeted questions system by system from head to toe
options.C: Ask the patient to list every illness they had as a child
options.D: Focus only on the exact organ system of the main complaint

explanation: Brilliant! Going step-by-step from the head down ensures you never accidentally leave out an important body system.

question: What is the defining feature of a Cost-Benefit Analysis in healthcare?

options.A: Outcomes are measured strictly in natural clinical units like blood pressure
options.B: Both costs and health outcomes are measured in monetary terms
options.C: It completely ignores financial expenses to focus on patient emotions
options.D: It is only used when two treatments produce identical results

explanation: In a Cost-Benefit Analysis, even the health outcomes are converted into money (like naira). This lets you directly compare cash spent to cash saved or earned.

question: Which of the following is a common health risk linked to traditional masculine norms?

options.A: Delayed diagnosis of chronic illnesses due to avoiding clinics
options.B: Increased biological vulnerability to hormonal imbalances
options.C: Strict social expectations to focus solely on domestic labor
options.D: Higher rates of maternal mortality during childbirth

explanation: Stoicism and the pressure to avoid showing weakness often prevent men from seeking early medical help, leading to delayed disease detection. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h7)

question: How would you best describe depression in a clinical setting?

options.A: A temporary lack of vitamins causing physical weakness
options.B: A minor behavioral adjustment issue in older adults
options.C: A serious mood disorder affecting thoughts and daily activities
options.D: A temporary emotional reaction to physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Depression isn't just a brief bad mood or fatigue; it's a true mood disorder that impacts a person's entire daily life and well-being.

question: Which of the following is a major barrier to safe motherhood in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of fully equipped emergency hospitals
options.B: Too many skilled midwives working in remote villages
options.C: Free transportation services for all pregnant women
options.D: Inadequate health infrastructure and out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Poor facilities and the burden of paying out-of-pocket for treatment prevent many Nigerian women from getting timely care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: Why must life-saving drugs like oxytocin be kept in a cold chain (refrigerated)?

options.A: Cold temperatures make the liquid solution taste much sweeter
options.B: Refrigeration prevents the glass ampoules from shattering
options.C: Freezing stops the plastic syringes from melting in storage
options.D: Heat exposure destroys the active potency of the medication

explanation: Exactly right! Uterotonics like oxytocin hate the heat; leaving them out in warm temperatures ruins their strength and effectiveness.

question: In nursing management, what does 'span of control' actually mean?

options.A: The number of workers who report directly to one manager
options.B: The total budget allocated to a nursing department
options.C: The physical size of the hospital building or ward
options.D: The number of clinical shifts a nurse works in a week

explanation: Think of span of control as 'how many direct reports does this boss have?' It counts the staff members under one specific leader.

question: Which of the following is an environmental hazard commonly checked during a home visit?

options.A: The type of flooring material in the kitchen
options.B: The color of paint used on the bedroom walls
options.C: Cluttered walkways and poor lighting
options.D: The brand of television in the living room

explanation: Physical hazards like clutter and poor lighting increase the risk of falls and injuries, especially for vulnerable clients. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which of these shows that a health advocacy campaign was truly successful?

options.A: The number of meetings held without reaching any agreement
options.B: A newly passed local health policy or increased service uptake
options.C: Increased complaints from hospital administrative staff
options.D: A reduction in the total number of community volunteers

explanation: Brilliant! Seeing actual policy changes or more people showing up to use health services proves your advocacy hard work paid off.

question: A patient offers you a costly birthday gift during a home visit. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Scold the patient harshly for trying to bribe clinical staff
options.B: Accept the gift quickly before other family members see it
options.C: Accept the gift but promise to bring an expensive present back
options.D: Politely decline the gift while thanking the patient for the kind thought

explanation: You got it! Refusing personal gifts kindly helps you maintain professional boundaries while still showing appreciation for the patient's warm intentions.

question: What is the big advantage of using the 'closed gloving' technique in theater?

options.A: It prevents bare hands from touching the outside of the sterile gloves
options.B: It eliminates the need to wear a surgical gown during the case
options.C: It keeps the sterile gloves warmer during long procedures
options.D: It allows the nurse to scrub hands much faster than usual

explanation: By keeping your hands tucked inside your gown sleeves, you can slide your gloves on without your bare skin ever touching the outside surface.
